question: The area of a rectangle remains unchanged when it is made \(2\dfrac12\) inches longer and \(\dfrac23\) inch narrower, or when it is made \(2\dfrac12\) inches shorter and \(\dfrac43\) inch wider. Its area, in square inches, is:
solution:
Let the original length and width be \(L\) and \(W\) inches. The shortened and narrowed rectangles must have positive dimensions, so \(L>5/2\) and \(W>2/3\).

Each modified rectangle has the original area \(LW\), giving
\[
\left(L+\frac52\right)\left(W-\frac23\right)=LW,
\]
\[
\left(L-\frac52\right)\left(W+\frac43\right)=LW.
\]
Expanding is useful because the shared term \(LW\) cancels. After cancellation and multiplication by \(6\), the equations become
\[
15W-4L=10,
\qquad
8L-15W=20.
\]
Adding eliminates \(W\), leaving \(4L=30\), so \(L=15/2\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(15W-30=10\), hence \(W=8/3\).

These dimensions satisfy the required positivity conditions. The modified dimensions are \(10\) by \(2\), and \(5\) by \(4\), so both modified areas are indeed \(20\). The original area is
\[
LW=\frac{15}{2}\cdot\frac83=20
\]
square inches, choice \(\mathrm{E}\).

edges.reason: After eliminating one unknown the procedure solves a one-variable linear equation; only this solving component is claimed.
Substitution introduces the reduction-to-one-variable idea, but adding equations to cancel an unknown is justified independently by equality operations.
The reduction and back-substitution leave one-variable linear equations that must be solved; this is not a claim that every route must name transposition.
A modeled two-equation system can be solved by addition/subtraction elimination instead of substitution; the optional method relation is correct.
Substitution can solve the modeled system without the addition/subtraction algorithm, so neither solving method should become a universal AND prerequisite.

The transferable model/solve/check workflow is useful preparation. Two-variable modeling can start directly with two relations, without completing a family of one-variable applications; Gemini's workflow overlap is not a mandatory earlier procedure.
edges.scope: general modeling workflow for word problems
